run_notes: Re-sourced the HDI pilot from directly fetched pages after discovering curl has open egress (the EGRESS_BLOCKED failures were WebFetch-specific). Material outcomes: (1) two pilot titles CORRECTED — Trevor Thomas is 'General Counsel and Secretary' not 'Corporate Secretary', and Bruce Jenkins has a formal EVP title identical to his HDI one; (2) Robert Dickinson's Amarc title and 2004 start year were unsupported by the live page and were dropped, keeping only what it actually says; (3) Amarc and Northern Dynasty addresses obtained — both 14th Floor, 1040 West Georgia, the same floor as Hunter Dickinson Acquisition Inc, with HDI on the 15th and Trekor on the 12th; (4) Amarc's published phone is identical to Hunter Dickinson Inc's, a shared switchboard and a stronger signal than shared premises; (5) the Taseko to Trekor Metals rename is confirmed against the live site; (6) one new cross-link found, Scott Cousens, HDI Director Capital Finance and an Amarc director. Known unresolved limitation: Trekor publishes 'Ronald W. Thiessen' and 'Robert A. Dickinson' with middle initials while the other sites omit them, and normalize_person deliberately refuses to merge across that difference. The graph therefore under-links these two people until a management information circular or insider ID resolves identity properly. That is the conservative failure mode working as designed, but it is a real recall cost and is the single strongest argument for moving to tier1_filing sourcing.
